reason: Both clear parts bend light, so they look like the starting pieces for the focusing front.
expectation: They will form a front section that focuses light.

effect: The cornea and lens now focus light toward the back; the iris still needs to control how much enters.
reaction: The ray diagram makes their shared focusing job clear.
reason: The iris has an opening that can narrow, so it belongs with the focusing front to control incoming light.
expectation: The iris will join the eye front and control the light entering it.

alternatives.reason: I could build the separate light-sensitive lining first.

effect: The eye front is complete: the iris controls incoming light, while the cornea and lens focus it.
reaction: The separate jobs of the iris and lens are clear.
reason: The light-sensitive cells and nerve cells are the visible pieces for the remaining lining and outgoing nerve.
expectation: They will form a light-sensitive lining connected to nerve fibres that carry signals away.

effect: The light-sensitive lining is the retina, and its outgoing bundle is the optic nerve. Both parts are ready to join the eye front.
reaction: Seeing how the nerve fibres gather into one bundle makes the connection clearer.
reason: The new goal calls for joining the completed focusing front and sensing lining.
expectation: They will form an eye with light focused onto the retina and signals leaving through the optic nerve.

effect: The completed eye shows light focused on the retina and signals travelling along the optic nerve toward the brain. All goals are complete.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the two separate builds come together.

mostWorthwhile.text: Joining the eye front and retina was most worthwhile because the finished cutaway connected focusing light with sending information toward the brain.

leastWorthwhile.text: Combining the cornea and lens was straightforward and predictable, though the ray diagram made their shared job clear.

surprise.text: I learned that the outgoing fibres gather into the optic nerve and that the light-sensitive lining is called the retina.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt particularly arbitrary; the pictures and goals explained why the pieces belonged together.

continue.text: I would probably continue: building the eye made its parts and their jobs understandable, and I would be curious to see another system assembled.
